findings.title: Reusing shut-down FixedQueuePool across rebalances silently drops all messages and commits their offsets
findings.body: `ResultsStrategyFactory.__init__` creates a single `self.queue_pool = FixedQueuePool(...)` instance, which `create_thread_queue_parallel_worker` passes to `SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy`. When Arroyo's `StreamProcessor` rebalances partitions, it calls ` close()`/`join()` (or `terminate()`) on the active strategy and then calls `factory.create_with_partitions(...)` for the new assignment. Because `SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.close()` and `terminate()` call `self.queue_pool.shutdown()`, all queues in `self.queue_pool` are permanently shut down (`q.shutdown()`) and all worker threads exit. On the subsequent `create_with_partitions` call, the factory reuses the same shut-down `self.queue_pool` (along with its stale `OffsetTracker` state). From that point on, every `work_queue.put(work_item)` call in `submit()` raises `queue.ShutDown` (a subclass of `Exception`), which `SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.submit()` catches in `except Exception:` (lines 317-325 of `queue_consumer.py`), logs, and marks as completed via `add_offset` + `complete_offset`—causing all messages after a rebalance to be dropped while their offsets are committed to Kafka.

findings.title: OffsetTracker.get_committable_offsets commits past offset gaps on the cycle after mark_committed
findings.body: In `OffsetTracker.get_committable_offsets()`, `start` is computed as `max(last_committed + 1, min_offset)`. Meanwhile, `mark_committed()` removes all offsets `<= offset` from `self.all_offsets[partition]`. If offsets `100`, `102`, and `103` finish while `101` has not been seen yet, the first call to `get_committable_offsets()` returns `100` (because `100` is in `all_offsets`, so `min_offset == 100`) and `mark_committed(partition, 100)` removes `100`, leaving `all_offsets = {102, 103}`. On the very next commit tick (1 second later, with `101` still missing), `min_offset` is now `102`, so `start = max(101, 102) = 102`, and the loop commits offset `103`, skipping right past the uncommitted gap at `101`. Once a partition has a `last_committed` value, `start` must be `last_committed + 1` rather than `max(last_committed + 1, min_offset)`.

findings.title: Shutdown drops queued items without draining and stops the commit thread before workers finish
findings.body:
There are two ordering bugs in the shutdown sequence:

1. `FixedQueuePool.shutdown()` sets `worker.shutdown = True` on all workers before calling `q.shutdown(immediate=False)`. Because `OrderedQueueWorker.run()` checks `while not self.shutdown:` on each loop iteration, workers exit as soon as they finish their current in-flight item instead of draining remaining queued items until `work_queue.get()` raises `queue.ShutDown`.
2. `SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.close()` sets `self.shutdown_event` and joins `self.commit_thread` *before* calling `self.queue_pool.shutdown()`, and never performs a final commit afterwards. Any offsets completed while workers finish in-flight items during shutdown (or after the last commit loop iteration) are never committed.

findings.title: Queues are unbounded and never apply backpressure to the Kafka consumer
findings.body: `SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy`'s docstring states that it provides "Natural backpressure when queues fill up", but `FixedQueuePool.__init__` creates each queue with `queue.Queue()` (`maxsize=0`, i.e. unbounded) and `SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.submit()` never raises Arroyo's `MessageRejected`. If worker threads fall behind Kafka polling (e.g. due to slow database/network calls), the consumer thread will buffer an unbounded number of work items—including the unused raw `WorkItem.message` payload—in memory.

findings.title: test_thread_queue_parallel_error_handling asserts that offsets were not committed and leaks commit threads
findings.body: `test_thread_queue_parallel_error_handling` states in its docstring: "Test that errors in processing don't block offset commits for other messages." Because `OrderedQueueWorker.run()` calls `complete_offset` in its `finally` block, both offset 100 (which raised an exception) and offset 101 (which succeeded) are marked complete and are committable. However, the test exits its wait loop after ~0.2s (before `SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy._commit_loop`'s 1.0s sleep elapses) and asserts `assert len(committed_offsets) == 0 or test_partition not in committed_offsets`—the opposite of the intended behavior, and flaky if the test takes >= 1s. Additionally, all of the `test_thread_queue_parallel*` tests in this file only call `factory.shutdown()` and never call `consumer.close()`, leaving `consumer.commit_thread` running in the background for the rest of the test process.

findings.title: Race condition in test_stats_reporting when workers drain items before get_stats() runs
findings.body: In `TestFixedQueuePool.test_stats_reporting`, 3 worker threads are already running a fast in-memory callback (`result_processor` only appends to a list) while the test loop submits 10 items. If the worker threads dequeue all 10 items before `stats = self.pool.get_stats()` executes on line 199, `stats["total_items"]` will be `0` and `assert stats["total_items"] > 0` will fail intermittently.
